name: CI
on:
  push: { branches: [main] }
  pull_request:
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: 20 }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck
      # The unit suite covers the Process Bar approval logic — the
      # human-oversight surface. It existed but was never gated here.
      - run: npm test
      - run: npm run build

# Mahlah

**Mahlah is a chat interface for your Tirzah memory, built to keep the answer
separate from the machinery behind it.** You see a clean conversational
reply. Beside it, what the system did to produce that answer is shown live:
retrieval, context selection, research, generation, and the running plan.

Mahlah is the front end that was split out of
[Tirzah](https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/tirzah). Tirzah does the memory,
retrieval and model work; Mahlah only presents it.

## Three channels, never mixed

1. **Answer:** the reply in the chat, rendered as markdown with a copy
   button. It never contains process scaffolding, chain-of-thought or
   database mechanics.
2. **Process:** a live panel showing what the system is doing for this
   request. When Tirzah runs a Deborah plan, the panel streams the plan as it
   executes, with construct badges (CALL, ITERATE, DECISION…) and step ids.
3. **Dev log:** the full, serial trace of the request lifecycle in a separate
   window (`⤢`), with history and live events and copy-as-JSON. It is
   suitable for a developer, or another AI assistant, to watch.

## Is it for you?

**Good fit:** you run Tirzah and want a familiar chat UI that also shows *how*
each answer was produced, plus human oversight of agentic work through the
Process Bar.

**Not a fit:** a standalone chatbot. Mahlah has no backend of its own and needs
a running Tirzah.

## Try it

```bash
tirzah serve                       # Tirzah's API on :8765
npm install && npm run dev         # Mahlah on http://localhost:5273
```

Mahlah proxies `/api` to `http://localhost:8765`; override with
`VITE_TIRZAH_API`. To skip the dev server, Tirzah can serve Mahlah's
production build itself: run `scripts/build_ui.sh` in Tirzah, and
`tirzah serve` then shows Mahlah on http://127.0.0.1:8765/. The model, adapter and retrieval-mode menus fill from
Tirzah's `/api/runtime`, so they show what is actually installed. The UI
defaults to an e-ink-friendly high-contrast theme.

## What you can do

- **Converse.** Conversations are auto-titled from the first prompt, and can
  be renamed or deleted. Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a new line.
- **Oversee agentic work with the Process Bar.** Bind a conversation to a
  human-defined process template (one is suggested from your first message),
  have Tirzah review a draft process, and approve or reject gate and
  deviation pauses as they come up. Failures show as a banner, never as
  silent no-ops.
- **Leave feedback** (`⚑`) tied to the current session and trace. It is
  stored as a record and as a `feedback.submitted` trace event.

## Know before you rely on it

- **Conversations are stored in this browser only** (localStorage, keyed by
  Tirzah's session id, capped in size). They do not sync between browsers or
  machines yet.
- Titles come from the first prompt, not from a model.


## Develop

```bash
npm test                           # vitest: Process Bar approval-state logic
npm run e2e                        # end-to-end against a real Tirzah
```

End-to-end answers wait up to 120 s by default, because Tirzah does real
memory work for each exchange (`MAHLAH_E2E_ANSWER_TIMEOUT`, in ms).

The endpoints Mahlah calls, with the response shape it relies on, are in
[docs/tirzah-api-contract.md](docs/tirzah-api-contract.md). Event types are
defined by [Galeed](https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/galeed) and served by
Tirzah. The [2026-08-11 review](docs/review-2026-08-11.md) findings are all
actioned.

*Mahlah is one of the daughters of Zelophehad, like her sisters Tirzah, Noa,
Hoglah and Milcah.*

# Mahlah — functional and code review **Date:** 2026-08-11 · **Reviewed:** `main` @ `33143c9`, package version **0.1.0** (clean working tree) **Actioned:** 2026-08-11. All findings implemented; 31 tests (was 4), and CI now gates them. See the CHANGELOG-equivalent notes in the commit. **Method:** the app was run against a live Tirzah backend on :8765 — proxy, `/api/runtime`, `/api/process/*` and a real `POST /api/ask` round trip — and the pure modules were probed adversarially with temporary vitest files. Every claim is backed by a run or a probe, reproduced inline. --- ## Part 1 — Functional review **Baseline:** `npm run typecheck` clean, `npm test` 4/4, `npm run build` succeeds. CI runs **typecheck and build only** — see F4. ### What works The full three-channel contract works end to end against a live backend: ``` app -> 200 proxy /api/runtime -> 200 proxy /api/process/* -> 200 POST /api/ask -> answer + 8 processEvents + traceId/sessionId/messageId ``` `/api/runtime` returns the live adapter and model set, so the composer dropdowns genuinely reflect what is installed rather than a hardcoded list. Two things deserve specific credit. **The markdown renderer's safety claim holds.** It says output is "React elements only (never raw HTML), so model output cannot inject markup". Probed with four attacks, all render as inert text: ``` raw HTML ->

Hello <img src=x onerror="alert(1)"> world

js link ->

[click](javascript:alert(1))

data: URL ->

[x](data:text/html;base64,PHNjcmlwdD4=)

HTTPS:// ->

[x](HTTPS://example.com)

(uppercase fails closed) ``` There is no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` anywhere, and the anchor path allows only `http://` / `https://` prefixes, so an unrecognised scheme degrades to plain text rather than becoming a link. For a surface that renders whatever a local model emits, that is exactly right, and the uppercase case failing *closed* rather than open is the detail that shows it was thought about. An unclosed code fence also degrades sensibly — the remaining text is kept inside the block rather than swallowed. **The localStorage load path is properly defensive.** It parses inside a `try`, rejects a non-array, then schema-checks every record and **salvages the valid ones** instead of dropping the lot, with a comment explaining why. That is better than most apps manage. Its counterpart, the save path, is not — see M2. ### Functional defects #### F1. A malformed trace entry crashes the approval surface — **FIXED** `pendingApproval` reads `last.detail.step_id` without checking that `detail` exists: ``` trace entry {event:'process.gate.reached', detail:{}} -> {"kind":"gate","stepId":"","text":"Gate at step ?."} trace entry {event:'process.gate.reached'} -> THREW: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'step_id') ``` The empty-object case was handled; the missing-key case was not. This runs during render of the Process Bar, so an older or malformed instance takes down the operator's approve/reject surface — the one control that exists to unblock paused agentic work, failing exactly when there is something to unblock. #### F2. Backend outages report a JSON parse error instead of the status — **FIXED** Five `/api/process/*` write calls use this shape: ```ts if (!res.ok) throw new Error((await res.json()).detail || `create failed: ${res.status}`) ``` The `||` fallback is unreachable when the error body is not JSON, because the throw happens *inside* `res.json()`. Probed: ``` 502 with an HTML body -> "Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0" 500 with an empty body -> "Unexpected end of JSON input" 400 with {"detail": …} -> "template name taken" (works as intended) ``` The README promises "API failures surface as an inline banner in the bar (not silent no-ops)", and they do surface — but a proxy 502 or a backend that died mid-session, which is the *likeliest* real failure, shows the operator a JSON-parsing message that reads like a client bug rather than "the backend is down". Affects `createProcessTemplate`, `startProcessInstance`, `resolveProcessGate`, `resolveProcessDeviation`, `completeProcessInstance`. #### F3. The documented `/api/ask` contract is a small subset of what arrives — **DOCUMENTED** The README documents four keys. The live response carries **30**: ``` activity_log, activity_report, adapter, answer, budget, controller_decision, conversation_domain_id, exchange_id, focus_node_id, messageId, model, ok, phase, plan_revisions, processEvents, process_run_id, process_trace, project_domain_id, query, replies…, requestId, request_plan, retrieval_status, semantic, semantic_diagnostic, semantic_status, semantic_summary, sessionId, session_id, traceId, used_node_ids ``` Not a defect — the extra fields are ignored harmlessly, and documenting the subset the UI consumes is a reasonable choice. Worth noting only because the README presents it as *the* contract, and several of those fields (`ok`, `retrieval_status`, `semantic_status`) are exactly the signals a UI would want if it ever wanted to say "retrieval found nothing" rather than rendering an ungrounded answer as though it were grounded. #### F4. CI does not run the tests — **FIXED** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`. It does not run `npm test`, so the vitest suite — the only automated check of the Process Bar approval logic, which is the human-oversight surface — is never gated. Mizpah's CI does run its tests; this one drifted. --- ## Part 2 — Code review ### Medium #### M1 · `processLogic.ts:22-29` — unguarded `detail` access — **FIXED** Code side of F1. `String(last.detail.step_id ?? '')` guards a missing *value* but not a missing *object*. **Fix:** `const detail = last.detail ?? {}` before use. The function is pure and already unit-tested, so the case costs one line and one test. #### M2 · `App.tsx:69-71` — the save path has none of the load path's care — **FIXED** ```ts useEffect(() => { localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(conversations)) }, [conversations]) ``` Unguarded, and conversations accumulate with their full message history — there is no cap on conversation count or message retention anywhere in the file. Once the store reaches its quota (typically 5–10 MB) `setItem` throws `QuotaExceededError` inside an effect, and persistence stops. The load path goes to real trouble to survive corrupt storage; the write that produces that storage has no equivalent. **Fix:** wrap in `try/catch`, surface a one-line warning when it fails, and cap retained history (oldest conversations, or messages per conversation). **Actioned.** Persistence moved to `src/storage.ts` so its failure paths are testable at all — the logic was unreachable from a test while it lived inside the component. Caps at 100 conversations / 200 messages each, retries with the newest 10 on quota, and surfaces a banner saying which degradation happened rather than stopping silently. #### M3 · `api.ts` — the error-body read should not be able to throw — **FIXED** Code side of F2, five call sites. **Fix:** one helper — ```ts async function errorMessage(res: Response, fallback: string): Promise { try { const body = await res.json() return body?.detail || fallback } catch { return fallback // non-JSON body: the status is the useful signal } } ``` ### Low #### L1 · `markdown.tsx:11` — inline tokens do not nest across types — **DOCUMENTED** `INLINE_TOKEN` splits on whole tokens, so `**bold with `code`**` renders the inner backticks literally. Correct and safe, just limited; worth a line in the module docstring listing what is deliberately not supported, since the current docstring reads as a capability list. #### L2 · README status claims `npm test` covers the Process Bar — **FIXED by F4** It does — 4 tests — but F4 means CI never runs them, so the claim is true of a developer's machine and not of the pipeline. --- ## Comparison with the other estate reviews Mahlah is the second-best documented frontend in the estate and the only one that ships a **verified** security property: the markdown renderer does what it claims under attack, which I tested rather than took on trust. Its two real defects are the estate's recurring shape once again, in the two places a UI can least afford them: - **F1** takes down the approval surface — the human-oversight control — when a trace entry is malformed. The failure is loud (a crash) rather than silent, which is better, but it lands on the one screen whose job is unblocking work. - **F2** is the silent-substitution version: the real signal (a 502, a dead backend) is replaced by a misleading one (a JSON syntax error). The operator is told something, just not the true thing — which is the same pattern as Hoglah replacing a real exception with `"Unexpected worker error"`, and Milcah replacing an adapter message with `"generation failed"`. The asymmetry in M2 is worth naming on its own: the code that *reads* persistence is carefully defensive about corruption, and the code that *writes* it has no handling at all. Defensive reading plus unguarded writing is a common shape, and it means the failure surfaces far from its cause. --- ## Suggested order 1. **M1** — one line and one test; it stops the oversight surface crashing. 2. **M3** — the `errorMessage` helper across five call sites, so an outage reads as an outage. 3. **F4** — add `npm test` to CI, so the Process Bar logic is actually gated. 4. **M2** — guard the write and cap retained history. 5. **F3, L1, L2** — documentation. Nothing here is architectural. The three-channel separation is real and works, the API layer is a clean single module, the renderer is safe, and the whole app is two runtime dependencies.

# Tirzah API contract (as consumed by Mahlah)

The parts of Tirzah's HTTP API that Mahlah calls, and the shape it relies on.
Moved from the root README (2026-10). Tirzah serves more routes than these;
this page lists only what Mahlah depends on.

## Endpoints Mahlah calls

Tirzah's backend returns the 3-channel contract:

- `POST /api/ask` →
  ```json
  {
    "answer": "clean conversational answer",
    "processEvents": [
      { "type": "retrieval.mongo.completed", "status": "ok",
        "summary": "Construct Retrieval Context", "trace_id": "trace_…",
        "session_id": "…", "seq": 3, "timestamp": "…", "metadata": {} }
    ],
    "traceId": "trace_…", "sessionId": "…", "messageId": "msg_…", "requestId": "req_…"
  }
  ```
  Those are the fields Mahlah consumes. The live response carries ~30 in total
  (including `ok`, `retrieval_status`, `semantic_status`, `process_trace`,
  `request_plan`); the extras are ignored. Worth knowing if the UI ever needs
  to distinguish "retrieval found nothing" from a confident-sounding answer.
- `GET /api/trace/stream?session_id=…|trace_id=…` — **SSE** live process/log stream
  (the process panel subscribes for the current request; the dev-log window
  subscribes with `replay=true` for history plus live events).
- `POST /api/feedback` — free-text feedback tied to the current `traceId`/`sessionId`
  (stored as a structured record **and** a `feedback.submitted` trace event).
- `GET /api/runtime` — adapters, models, and retrieval modes for the composer
  dropdowns.

## Process Bar (`/api/process/*`)

The **Process Bar** above the composer is the human-oversight surface for
agentic work. It binds a conversation to a human-defined process template,
auto-suggests a fit from the first message, and surfaces gate / deviation
pauses for approve/reject.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/process/templates` | List presets + saved templates |
| `POST` | `/api/process/templates` | Create a template (`name`, `body`, …) |
| `POST` | `/api/process/suggest` | Suggest a template for a task string |
| `POST` | `/api/process/review` | Tirzah review of a draft process body |
| `GET` | `/api/process/active?session_id=…` | Active instance for the session (404 → none) |
| `POST` | `/api/process/instances` | Start an instance on a session |
| `POST` | `/api/process/instances/{id}/gate` | Approve/reject a gate step |
| `POST` | `/api/process/instances/{id}/deviation/resolve` | Resolve a deviation |
| `POST` | `/api/process/instances/{id}/complete` | Mark the instance complete |

API failures surface as an inline banner in the bar (not silent no-ops).

Structured event types are stable and extensible: `session.created`,
`message.user.submitted`, `process.started`, `retrieval.mongo.*`,
`context.selected`, `research.*`, `model.prompt.built`, `model.response.*`,
`answer.finalized`, `log.persisted`, `feedback.submitted`, … (defined by
Galeed, with Tirzah currently serving the HTTP/SSE trace API).

  "name": "mahlah",
  "private": true,
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "type": "module",
  "description": "Conversational web interface for the Tirzah memory engine",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "vite",
    "build": "tsc && vite build",
    "preview": "vite preview",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "test": "vitest run",
    "e2e": "node e2e/run.mjs",
    "shot": "node e2e/shot.mjs"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^18.3.1",
    "react-dom": "^18.3.1"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/react": "^18.3.5",
    "@types/react-dom": "^18.3.0",
    "@vitejs/plugin-react": "^4.3.1",
    "playwright": "^1.61.1",
    "typescript": "^5.5.4",
    "vite": "^5.4.2",
    "vitest": "^1.6.1"
  }
}

{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "lib": ["ES2020", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"],
    "module": "ESNext",
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "strict": true,
    "noUnusedLocals": true,
    "noUnusedParameters": true,
    "noFallthroughCasesInSwitch": true
  },
  "include": ["src"]
}
